scope: A depth audit for independent work on this UIKit/SwiftUI client, informed by your Kotlin/Java experience. The original 28 core sessions are joined by 28 deep dives. Topic names are not a claim to cover every Apple API; use the evidence column to turn reading into demonstrated engineering skill.
limitations: Coverage describes explanations and available exercises, not completed learner work. Your previous notes, quiz answers, and pending exercises are preserved.
No production app build, device performance measurement, accessibility audit, distribution action, or platform migration is established by this material.
Repository anchors are checked against this checkout. Toolchain pins, deployment targets, build graphs, library behavior, and Apple policies must be rechecked when implementing a change.
Specialist branches are explicitly listed rather than hidden. They need dedicated projects, devices, official documentation, and specialist review where appropriate.
The course remains local and offline for reading. Online references need a connection; browser progress is not automatically synchronized with mentor feedback or the Markdown log.

groups.title: Swift language and API design
groups.summary: Understand the syntax and semantics that determine a public contract, not merely the Kotlin spelling of each keyword.

topics.title: Bindings, properties, access and initialization
topics.detail: let/var, numeric widths and labels; memberwise/public/designated/convenience/required/failable initialization; visibility, property observers and lazy initialization are expanded in the Swift detail guide.
topics.evidence: Translate a nullable model, predict mutation, and explain which module can construct or subclass its exported type.

topics.title: Optional handling and domain absence
topics.detail: nil, if let, guard let, chaining, fallback and traps; absent, empty and failed are separate product outcomes.
topics.evidence: Handle absent input, empty successful results and failures without force unwraps or lost distinctions.

topics.title: Enums, raw values and pattern matching
topics.detail: Associated payloads, contextual dot syntax, exhaustive switches and raw identifiers differ from subclass-based sealed hierarchies.
topics.evidence: Add a state and explain the required handling decisions exposed by the compiler.

topics.title: Protocols, generics, associated types and dispatch
topics.detail: Requirements, default behavior, extension-only methods, associated types and where constraints; any versus some versus preserving a generic concrete type, visibility and module boundaries.
topics.evidence: Substitute a fake, preserve an associated output relationship and explain implementation selection through a protocol contract.

topics.title: Closures, errors and callback ownership
topics.detail: Function types, trailing closures, @escaping, captures, throws, try/do/catch, try?, defer and cancellation as a separate effect. The detail guide contrasts delegates, observer tokens, GCD and Swift task ownership.
topics.evidence: Preserve outcomes and show observer cleanup, callback delivery context and task/queue ownership separately.

topics.title: Collections, value semantics and algorithm cost
topics.detail: Array/dictionary values, nested references, copy-on-write, allocation behavior and the cost of repeated transformations.
topics.evidence: Explain aliasing and compare full-value-correct algorithms under a stated workload.

topics.title: Property wrappers, result builders and macros
topics.detail: State/Binding projection, Observation generation and SwiftUI builders are different mechanisms; syntax does not imply persistence or actor safety.
topics.evidence: Identify the generated contract and deployment/toolchain requirement of each annotation in a small view.

topics.title: Objective-C interoperability
topics.detail: NSObject boundaries, selectors, dynamic dispatch and bridging introduce contracts distinct from Swift value and actor semantics.
topics.evidence: Trace a bridged delegate/callback and explain ownership, dispatch and string or collection conversion.

topics.title: Compiler, language mode and API availability
topics.detail: Compiler version, Swift tools-version, language mode, SDK and minimum OS are independent axes, including Swift concurrency checking.
topics.evidence: Read effective target settings and distinguish a language diagnostic from an unavailable platform API.

groups.title: Ownership and concurrency
groups.summary: Design who owns state and work, when work stops, and what may change across suspension.

topics.title: ARC and retain-cycle graphs
topics.detail: Strong, weak and unowned ownership; stored closures, delegates, subscriptions, tasks and deinitialization.
topics.evidence: Reproduce a cycle, prove release after correction, and explain why a nested strong task is not automatically a permanent cycle.

topics.title: Task ownership and cancellation
topics.detail: View-associated versus unstructured tasks, retained handles, stopping events, CancellationError and cooperative checks.
topics.evidence: Leave a screen during work and prove that cancellation cannot publish an irrelevant result.

topics.title: Structured and bounded parallelism
topics.detail: async let, throwing task groups, output ordering, concurrency caps and error policy; task creation is not a free optimization.
topics.evidence: Use controlled dependencies to verify order, maximum work in flight and parent cancellation.

topics.title: Actors, reentrancy and stale results
topics.detail: Isolation prevents data races, not business races across await. Account and request generations protect different invariants.
topics.evidence: Complete a stale load after reset/logout and prove it cannot replace current account state.

topics.title: MainActor, Sendable and executor behavior
topics.detail: UI isolation, closure transfer safety, unchecked annotations and version-dependent nonisolated async behavior; await is not a background-thread promise.
topics.evidence: Draw isolation boundaries and justify where expensive synchronous work actually executes.

topics.title: AsyncSequence, Combine, ReactiveKit and Flow
topics.detail: Hot/cold behavior, replay, demand, buffering, subscription lifetime, completion and bridge semantics are not one-to-one mappings. Core lesson 017 retains conceptual RxSwift comparisons; 045 corrects the guide's claim using the active ReactiveKit declaration/export.
topics.evidence: Specify the contract of a bridge and test cancellation, dropped values and error propagation.

topics.title: Shared work and per-consumer cancellation
topics.detail: Service-owned refresh/cache work may outlive a screen; canceling one waiter must not silently invalidate other consumers.
topics.evidence: Write separate policies for waiter cancellation, logout and completion of shared work.

topics.title: Legacy async migration seams
topics.detail: PromiseKit/ReactiveKit/Combine coexist with native concurrency; adapters must preserve error, lifetime and event semantics. Guidance alone does not prove migration or an active RxSwift dependency.
topics.evidence: Propose an incremental adapter with explicit compatibility tests instead of a whole-app rewrite.

groups.title: UIKit engineering
groups.summary: Layout, ownership and reuse are contracts that need testing under changing content and window conditions.

topics.title: Controller lifecycle and containment
topics.detail: View loading, appearance, visibility, navigation and deallocation differ. Child-controller containment requires a complete sequence.
topics.evidence: Trace ownership and appearance during push, pop, modal dismissal and hosted content.

topics.title: Auto Layout constraints and priorities
topics.detail: Intrinsic size, hugging, compression resistance, required versus optional constraints and ambiguity are not simple width/height settings.
topics.evidence: Repair an ambiguous/conflicting layout and justify priorities with long text and narrow widths.

topics.title: Safe areas, traits and adaptive sizing
topics.detail: Safe areas, readable/content guides, size-class changes and dynamic text must be reasoned about at the current window size.
topics.evidence: Verify large text, safe-area changes and resized windows without duplicated inset ownership.

topics.title: Table and collection reuse
topics.detail: Stable model identifiers, reusable cell reset, deferred responses and cancellation must not let an old item update a new cell.
topics.evidence: Reuse a cell during delayed image loading and prove the visible item remains correct.

topics.title: Diffable snapshots and compositional layout
topics.detail: Snapshot identifiers, model lookup, reconfiguration, section identity and layout sizing have separate responsibilities.
topics.evidence: Insert, remove and update items without index-based identity or lost selections.

topics.title: Pagination, prefetch and scroll state
topics.detail: Deduplication, page ownership, stale query rejection, prefetch cancellation and scroll anchoring are product rules.
topics.evidence: Rapidly change query and page requests, then test no duplicates or stale rows.

topics.title: Text input and keyboard layout
topics.detail: First responder, keyboard avoidance, selection/cursor behavior, composing text and focus transitions affect real editing.
topics.evidence: Edit with hardware/software keyboards and composed input without losing focus, text or cursor position.

topics.title: Interactions and animation lifetime
topics.detail: Gesture conflicts, interruption, state commits and reduced-motion policy require explicit decisions.
topics.evidence: Interrupt an animation or rapid gesture and explain the resulting state and accessible action.

topics.title: Design-system component contracts
topics.detail: Prefer active ZDUI/ZDComponent APIs and resource ownership over unrelated tutorial components; styles must adapt to traits and text.
topics.evidence: Trace one component's state, resources, typography, accessibility and module boundary.

groups.title: SwiftUI engineering
groups.summary: View descriptions, identity, observation and geometry must remain separate from side effects and persistence.

topics.title: State ownership and view identity
topics.detail: State, Binding, Bindable, StateObject, ObservedObject and environment distribution answer different questions.
topics.evidence: Preserve a draft during rerendering and deliberately reset only its intended identity.

topics.title: Layout proposals and modifier order
topics.detail: Parent proposals, child measurement and placement; padding/frame/background order changes the layout and drawing contract.
topics.evidence: Explain a layout's measured size and repair truncation at large text sizes without arbitrary fixed frames.

topics.title: Custom Layout, geometry and preferences
topics.detail: Measurement and preferences are scoped data flow, not unrestricted imperative layout; feedback can create update loops.
topics.evidence: Describe one-way measurement flow and identify a geometry-to-state feedback loop before adding a custom layout.

topics.title: Result builders, styles and environment
topics.detail: Opaque some View, conditional descriptions, inherited environment values and reusable styles need clear type and ownership boundaries.
topics.evidence: Explain what the builder constructs and which environment/style input determines the displayed control.

topics.title: Navigation, sheets and bridge updates
topics.detail: Typed routes, path state, modal dismissal scope, representable creation/update and coordinator lifetime.
topics.evidence: Verify every terminal path and bridge update, including user-driven dismissals.

topics.title: Transactions, gestures and focus
topics.detail: Animation intent, repeated actions, gesture arbitration, focus state and accessibility should share the same product state.
topics.evidence: Test rapid input and interruption while maintaining one correct state owner.

topics.title: Observation and rendering cost
topics.detail: Property reads, identity churn, expensive body work and repeated transformations affect invalidation and frame completion.
topics.evidence: Measure a representative update and isolate invalidation from rendering, layout and asynchronous work.

topics.title: Lists, lazy containers and scroll identity
topics.detail: Stable identifiers, item reuse expectations, state location and scroll/focus restoration must be tested with changing data.
topics.evidence: Update and reorder a list while preserving the intended edit, selection and scroll state.

groups.title: Application lifecycle and adaptive UI
groups.summary: An application, a scene, a controller and a task have different lifetimes; iOS is not Android recreation with renamed callbacks.

topics.title: App/scene lifecycle and multiple windows
topics.detail: Composition roots, scene activity, scene-owned navigation and shared account services require explicit lifetime boundaries.
topics.evidence: Draw owners and event transitions for two scenes and for leaving/returning to the app.

topics.title: Restoration versus persistent state
topics.detail: In-memory drafts, scene restoration, saved user data and server truth are separate promises across process termination.
topics.evidence: State exactly what survives navigation, identity reset, scene destruction and process restart.

topics.title: iPad and resizable window behavior
topics.detail: Window geometry, size classes, split layouts, pointer/keyboard input and deployment/device-family settings are distinct.
topics.evidence: Inspect actual supported device families and test adaptive layouts without claiming unimplemented tablet support.

topics.title: VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and focus
topics.detail: Semantic labels, traits, grouping, reading order, paragraph geometry and accessible actions need device task checks.
topics.evidence: Complete a user task with VoiceOver and large text; attach observed failures and corrections.

topics.title: Localization, right-to-left and appearance
topics.detail: Long translations, bidirectional content, locale-aware formatting, dark/high-contrast colors and reduced motion are separate axes.
topics.evidence: Test a locale/appearance matrix and explain logical versus physical direction and semantic colors.

topics.title: OS availability and graceful fallbacks
topics.detail: Compile-time API availability and runtime capability/authorization are not the same as a minimum deployment target.
topics.evidence: Document the unavailable-API and denied-capability branches for a representative feature.

groups.title: Networking and data contracts
groups.summary: Transport, decoding, authentication, caching and domain interpretation are independent failure boundaries.

topics.title: URLSession and HTTP validation
topics.detail: Request construction, headers, transport errors, status validation and representation expectations precede decoding.
topics.evidence: Verify status errors win over malformed error bodies and cancellation stays observable.

topics.title: Codable and compatibility
topics.detail: CodingKeys, missing/null/wrong-type fields, dates, enums, schema evolution and DTO-to-domain mapping.
topics.evidence: Keep fixtures for omitted, null, valid and malformed values and justify fallback policy.

topics.title: Authentication and refresh ownership
topics.detail: Trusted hosts, HTTPS, existing headers, shared refresh, bounded retries and stale account completion guards.
topics.evidence: Explain concurrent refresh, canceled waiters and logout without token leakage or credential resurrection.

topics.title: Retries, deadlines and idempotency
topics.detail: Replayable bodies, stable logical-operation keys, attempt caps, jitter and cancellation; a timeout does not prove a write failed.
topics.evidence: Design replay policy for a read and a non-idempotent write, including ambiguous timeout outcomes.

topics.title: HTTP and domain cache correctness
topics.detail: Freshness, ETag/conditional requests, memory/disk budgets and account/query identity need one coherent policy.
topics.evidence: Test cold/warm, invalidation, stale completion and account changes without serving another account's data.

topics.title: GraphQL and generated API contracts
topics.detail: Inspect current generated operations and generators; generated code does not remove domain, nullability or regeneration responsibilities.
topics.evidence: Trace a generated type to its schema/source, regeneration command and consuming public boundary.

topics.title: Streaming, response sizes and backpressure
topics.detail: Buffered response APIs differ from incremental delivery; buffering policy must match replaceable state versus required events.
topics.evidence: Specify a maximum response/buffer budget and prove a canceled consumer stops the intended work.

topics.title: Offline behavior and user recovery
topics.detail: Transport failures, empty success, cancellation, expired authorization and stale displayed data need separate user actions.
topics.evidence: Write and test the state transition for each failure and for retry after connectivity returns.

groups.title: Persistence and Foundation correctness
groups.summary: Small date, text and file assumptions can become data corruption, cross-account leakage or user-visible failures.

topics.title: Preferences, secrets, durable data and caches
topics.detail: UserDefaults, Keychain, files and databases have different durability, access, security and eviction contracts.
topics.evidence: Classify each stored field and specify logout, protection, failure and migration behavior.

topics.title: Core Data contexts and object identity
topics.detail: Context queue confinement, object IDs, fetching, saving, background work, merges and transaction scope are not Room DAO semantics.
topics.evidence: Move an object ID rather than a managed object across context boundaries and verify save/merge behavior.

topics.title: SwiftData, model evolution and migration
topics.detail: Availability, ModelContext ownership, schema change and rollback/data compatibility need a versioned plan.
topics.evidence: Produce migration fixtures and an upgrade/failure plan before adopting a persistence framework.

topics.title: Dates, calendars, zones and DST
topics.detail: An instant, provider-local appointment, calendar date and user-formatted label are not interchangeable. Ambiguous/nonexistent local times need policy.
topics.evidence: Test zone changes and DST gaps/folds while preserving the appointment's domain meaning.

topics.title: Unicode, string indices and text editing
topics.detail: Grapheme clusters, UTF-16/code units, normalization, substring indices and composing input have different length and editing semantics.
topics.evidence: Use emoji/combining/IME fixtures and explain the API's required representation instead of assuming integer offsets.

topics.title: Locale, numbers and decimal meaning
topics.detail: Display formatting, localized parsing and exact domain arithmetic differ; locale is not a time zone or a fixed wire format.
topics.evidence: Separate a stable wire value from user formatting and test at least two locale conventions.

topics.title: Sandbox directories and protected files
topics.detail: Documents/support/caches/temporary locations, backup policy, protection, atomic replacement and scoped access each carry distinct promises.
topics.evidence: Explain file location, access while locked, cleanup, extension sharing and interrupted-write recovery.

topics.title: Account scoping and invalidation
topics.detail: Key names, database ownership, cookies and cached snapshots must not outlive the intended account boundary.
topics.evidence: Switch accounts during an in-flight load and inspect all local state that must be cleared or retained.

groups.title: Build variants, targets and tooling
groups.summary: Treat an iOS build as a reproducible graph with distinct actions and configuration layers, not as a renamed Gradle flavor.

topics.title: Targets, schemes and configurations
topics.detail: A target defines a buildable unit; a scheme selects actions/configurations; configuration values are not Android product flavors.
topics.evidence: Map the build, test, run and archive actions to their actual target and configuration.

topics.title: xcconfig and effective settings
topics.detail: Includes, inherited values, overrides, environment settings and Info.plist substitution must be traced to effective results.
topics.evidence: Trace a synthetic setting through layers and detect a configuration that silently selects the wrong environment.

topics.title: Bundle IDs, signing and capabilities
topics.detail: App/extension identifiers, entitlements, certificate/profile inputs and APNs environments must align; no secret values belong in course examples.
topics.evidence: Create an identity/capability ledger and distinguish simulator, device, beta and store validation.

topics.title: Build configurations versus runtime flags
topics.detail: Compile-time inclusion, DEBUG conditionals, distribution identity and remotely assigned variants operate on separate control planes.
topics.evidence: Explain which change needs a binary release and what an offline/cached flag can or cannot contain.

topics.title: Sources, targets and resource membership
topics.detail: Files in the navigator, imports, filesystem-synchronized groups, SPM targets and resource bundles do not automatically describe the same graph.
topics.evidence: Prove where a source/resource is compiled/copied and who can import or load it.

topics.title: Tuist/SPM migration and graph parity
topics.detail: Legacy and generated manifests coexist. Dependency edits need the established synchronization path, not an assumed completed migration.
topics.evidence: Compare both manifests and CI paths for a bounded dependency without editing production during the course.

topics.title: Incremental builds and compiler optimization
topics.detail: Type checking, dependency invalidation, compilation mode, optimization settings and linking must be measured separately.
topics.evidence: Benchmark one isolated build hypothesis with fixed tools, caches and output equivalence.

topics.title: Destinations, test hosts and architectures
topics.detail: Simulator/device architectures, deployment availability, test-host linkage and signing determine which verification can run.
topics.evidence: Choose a test destination and identify a host, architecture or entitlement mismatch from diagnostics.

topics.title: LLDB and diagnostic tools
topics.detail: Breakpoints, stack frames, values, view hierarchy, Main Thread Checker, Thread Sanitizer, symbols and targeted cache diagnosis.
topics.evidence: Classify and reproduce a small failure, retaining matching symbols and useful diagnostic evidence.

groups.title: Libraries, modules and resources
groups.summary: Know what each dependency owns, why it exists, how it is linked, and what its removal or upgrade would change.

topics.title: SPM packages, products, targets and pins
topics.detail: Declared requirements, resolved transitive versions, products and target dependencies are distinct objects in the dependency graph.
topics.evidence: Trace a dependency from requirement to resolved pin to importing target and test its public behavior.

topics.title: Verified active library landscape
topics.detail: Inventory networking, reactive, image, analytics/diagnostic, testing and integration dependencies from active manifests and call sites, not legacy copies.
topics.evidence: Record each selected library's role, owner/lifetime, consuming target and replacement risk.

topics.title: ZDModules and internal boundaries
topics.detail: Protocol factories, DIResolver, feature/infra separation and composition roots choose dependencies and lifetimes.
topics.evidence: Trace one public contract through composition, implementation, consumer and fake.

topics.title: Static/dynamic linkage and XCFrameworks
topics.detail: Link-time/runtime loading, slices, ABI and module stability, resources and deployment requirements need separate checks.
topics.evidence: Explain a binary dependency's supported slices, runtime loading and compiler/module compatibility assumptions.

topics.title: Supply chain, licenses and upgrades
topics.detail: Provenance, license obligations, vulnerability response, transitive changes and removed public APIs are part of library ownership.
topics.evidence: Write a bounded dependency upgrade plan with compatibility checks, review gates and recovery.

topics.title: Code generation and reproducibility
topics.detail: Schemas, generators, plugins/scripts, generated sources and version pins must produce a traceable artifact; generated edits are not a durable fix.
topics.evidence: Identify inputs, tool pins, invocation and consuming target; explain how to verify a regeneration diff.

topics.title: Assets, localization and module bundles
topics.detail: Asset catalogs, strings/catalogs, generated accessors, package bundles and framework resources have explicit lookup ownership.
topics.evidence: Trace a resource from source to archive inclusion and load it through the correct module bundle.

topics.title: Privacy manifests and archive resources
topics.detail: Declared privacy information, SDK resources and actual data behavior are related but not interchangeable compliance evidence.
topics.evidence: Inspect relevant declarations and the built artifact; do not claim a manifest alone establishes policy compliance.

groups.title: Performance and optimization
groups.summary: Measure a user-visible scenario, isolate a cause, preserve correctness, and add a regression guard before claiming improvement.

topics.title: Measurement contracts and distributions
topics.detail: Scenario definition, device/build/toolchain, workload, cold/warm conditions, repeated samples, p50/p95 and confounding variables.
topics.evidence: Write a reproducible baseline/report and distinguish observations from untested hypotheses.

topics.title: Instruments, signposts and production signals
topics.detail: CPU/allocations/hitches/energy traces, interval boundaries, matching symbols and MetricKit-style fleet context answer different questions.
topics.evidence: Correlate a bounded trace with a defined user action and explain its limits.

topics.title: Launch and first usable frame
topics.detail: Pre-main/loading, initializer work, app/scene setup, dependency startup and first draw are not one launch number.
topics.evidence: Separate cold/warm launches and identify the milestone that represents usable UI.

topics.title: Binary, resources and installed size
topics.detail: Dependency/linking choices, resources, code inclusion and delivered versus installed sizes need artifact evidence.
topics.evidence: Compare matching release artifacts and justify a removal without discarding required resources or behavior.

topics.title: Frame pipeline and scrolling hitches
topics.detail: Refresh cadence is not a universal main-thread allowance. Layout, commits, drawing, GPU work and scheduling affect completed frames.
topics.evidence: Reproduce scrolling hitches on a representative device and isolate repeated main-thread work.

topics.title: SwiftUI identity and invalidation costs
topics.detail: Expensive body work, broad reads, unstable IDs and repeated transforms can inflate update work; visibility alone does not explain cost.
topics.evidence: Measure and reduce a specific update path without losing identity or state correctness.

topics.title: Memory graphs, ARC and copy-on-write
topics.detail: Retained ownership, temporary allocations, bridged collections, autorelease pools, footprint and termination are distinct investigations.
topics.evidence: Compare repeat-open/close behavior, retained objects and peak footprint; explain a surviving reference graph.

topics.title: Image decoding, downsampling and caching
topics.detail: Compressed file size differs from decoded pixel memory. Target pixel dimensions, scale, decoding, reuse and cost-bounded caches matter.
topics.evidence: Calculate decoded memory, preserve image quality at target size and reject stale image updates.

topics.title: Concurrency, IO and scheduling cost
topics.detail: Task caps, priorities, batching, cancellation, streaming and buffer budgets require workload-aware tradeoffs, not unlimited parallelism.
topics.evidence: Record in-flight work, memory and completion ordering while canceling or changing inputs.

topics.title: Energy, thermal pressure, network and cache efficiency
topics.detail: Repeated requests, wakeups, radio/IO work, thermal state, Low Power Mode, memory-pressure reactions, freshness and background execution must balance user latency and resource cost.
topics.evidence: Specify a resource-aware cache/network policy and collect representative evidence rather than promising battery savings from source changes.

topics.title: Algorithms, generics and build performance
topics.detail: Asymptotic cost, allocation, dispatch/bridging and compiler/linker settings should be profiled separately while preserving full output meaning.
topics.evidence: Compare an isolated algorithm/build hypothesis with equivalence fixtures and fixed measurement conditions.

topics.title: Regression gates and rollout validation
topics.detail: A faster microbenchmark does not prove faster user interaction; choose tolerances, noisy environments, compatibility and operational metrics.
topics.evidence: Attach correctness tests, a reproducible before/after report and a gate tied to the original user symptom.

groups.title: Platform services and boundaries
groups.summary: Permissions, capabilities, scheduling, extensions and trust boundaries determine what a feature can actually do.

topics.title: Background execution and scheduling
topics.detail: Finite foreground-to-background work, background task requests, cancellation and expiration differ from guaranteed timers or permanent services.
topics.evidence: Write foreground/background/expiration/termination branches without promising exact execution times.

topics.title: Notifications and APNs
topics.detail: Authorization, token/environment, entitlement, foreground delivery and remote/silent payload handling are separate contracts.
topics.evidence: Map denied authorization, token change, foreground delivery and route handling; never place tokens or private payloads in logs.

topics.title: Deep links, universal links and App Clips
topics.detail: Association/routing, URL validation, authentication gates, duplicate delivery and scene selection require a safe navigation policy.
topics.evidence: Test malformed/untrusted/duplicate links and pre-auth versus post-auth routing with one valid destination.

topics.title: WKWebView and system authentication
topics.detail: Navigation policies, scripts/messages, cookies, session ownership and system browser authentication should not share hidden trust assumptions.
topics.evidence: Draw the trust boundary and reject untrusted redirects/messages while cleaning up retained bridge handlers.

topics.title: Permissions and capability states
topics.detail: Not determined, authorized, denied, restricted and limited states differ by framework; hardware and OS availability are separate.
topics.evidence: Test denial/revocation/unavailable capability and provide a useful fallback without repeated permission prompts.

topics.title: Location, maps, photos and camera basics
topics.detail: Service ownership, callbacks, permission policy, limited access, selection and capture lifetimes are introduced; full media pipelines are a specialist branch.
topics.evidence: Specify capability lifetime and fallback policy, and trace a representative active integration.

topics.title: Extensions, widgets and App Intents
topics.detail: Separate executable/process/configuration, shared data, timeline or intent contracts and privacy limits differ from an in-app screen.
topics.evidence: Map one extension's target, resource/signing, shared-data and update boundaries without assuming a persistent process.

topics.title: Cross-platform integration review
topics.detail: Account state, deep links, notifications, persistence and extension updates cross multiple owners and must remain consistent.
topics.evidence: Produce an event/state/ownership matrix and test one delayed event after account or scene changes.

groups.title: Testing, security, reliability and release
groups.summary: A feature is deliverable only when its behavior, failure handling, artifact identity and recovery boundaries are reviewable.

topics.title: XCTest and Swift Testing
topics.detail: Discovery, assertions, optional checks, parameterization, isolation and test-target conventions vary by framework and target.
topics.evidence: Write behavior tests for success, empty, failure and invalid inputs; attach what actually ran.

topics.title: Deterministic asynchronous tests
topics.detail: Controlled completion/clocks and interleavings prove cancellation and stale-result policy better than arbitrary sleep durations.
topics.evidence: Complete competing operations in both orders and verify the product invariant.

topics.title: Snapshots, UI tests and accessibility evidence
topics.detail: Visual contracts, actual interactions, semantics, Dynamic Type and device audits are complementary rather than interchangeable.
topics.evidence: Build a behavior/locale/text-size matrix with explicit manual/device gaps.

topics.title: Observability, crash symbols and impact
topics.detail: Matching dSYMs/build identity, controlled diagnostic context, incidents, metrics and denominator-based impact matter.
topics.evidence: Write an incident hypothesis tied to a matching build and separate volume from affected-user rate.

topics.title: Security and privacy threat modeling
topics.detail: Keychain, ATS, host validation, permissions, minimal data, log redaction and SDK behavior need concrete assets and trust boundaries.
topics.evidence: Map assets/attackers/boundaries and validate a mitigated failure with synthetic data only.

topics.title: CI and verification matrices
topics.detail: Target/configuration/destination/host matrices, pins, generated graphs, result bundles and cache conditions determine reproducibility.
topics.evidence: Choose the smallest relevant verification and state what it cannot establish.

topics.title: Signing, beta and distribution artifacts
topics.detail: Install, archive, upload, processing, review and availability are distinct stages; version/build/binary UUIDs and symbols must be traceable.
topics.evidence: Create a synthetic release ledger including clean install, upgrade and symbol checks.

topics.title: Rollout, containment and recovery
topics.detail: Phased store distribution, runtime flag cohorts, backward-compatible services and corrective releases are different operations.
topics.evidence: Handle a launch failure before flags load without promising installed-client downgrades.

topics.title: Dependency, API and data upgrades
topics.detail: Old/new clients, schema fixtures, transitive dependency changes, minimum OS and rollback constraints need explicit compatibility evidence.
topics.evidence: Plan one bounded change with compatibility gates, owners and a recoverable rollout.

groups.title: Architecture and staff-level practice
groups.summary: Learning platform APIs is a foundation; independent judgment and repeated delivery make it useful to a team.

topics.title: Vertical feature traces and ownership maps
topics.detail: Follow one action from entry through contract, state, dependencies, UI, tests and terminal cleanup; verify active target membership.
topics.evidence: Give a reviewer a reproducible trace with unresolved assumptions explicitly marked.

topics.title: RFCs and architectural alternatives
topics.detail: Contract, alternatives, measurable outcome, migration seams, ownership, cost and reversal conditions belong in a decision.
topics.evidence: Defend a bounded proposal and state evidence that would reverse your recommendation.

topics.title: Incremental migration and rollout
topics.detail: Adapters and compatibility seams should preserve callers while reducing risk; neither a library upgrade nor a new wrapper proves migration complete.
topics.evidence: Define stages, parity tests, deprecation conditions and recovery responsibilities.

topics.title: Portfolio and competency gates
topics.detail: Planned, observed and reproduced evidence differ from production impact. Reading or self-reviewed checkboxes are not mentor certification.
topics.evidence: Attach tests, traces, measured artifacts and reviewer feedback without inventing outcomes.

topics.title: Mentoring and cross-platform influence
topics.detail: Share product contracts and measurement methods where useful; platform implementation and lifecycle rules may remain native.
topics.evidence: Have another engineer reproduce an artifact and record what needs clearer explanation.

topics.title: Learning feedback and next responsibilities
topics.detail: The reader supplies lesson quizzes, an interview attempt/feedback ledger, manual review dates and mixed-quiz history. Mentor acceptance, automatic adaptive recall, scheduled review notifications and automatic Markdown-log synchronization are not implemented.
topics.evidence: Submit actual exercise or interview-answer evidence for independent review and choose the next task from demonstrated gaps, not only the last browsed page.

groups.title: Specialist branches still to study
groups.summary: These are real parts of Apple's ecosystem. Naming them here is a boundary, not a claim that a general mobile course teaches them to production depth.

topics.title: Metal, advanced graphics and GPU optimization
topics.detail: Custom GPU shaders, frame capture, resource synchronization and graphics pipelines require a dedicated project and device profiling.
topics.evidence: Build and profile a small GPU workload with graphics-specific correctness and performance review.

topics.title: Real-time audio/video and capture pipelines
topics.detail: AVAudioSession routing, interruptions, AVFoundation pipelines, codecs, DSP and live-call quality need specialist lifecycle/network/device work.
topics.evidence: Run interruption, route-change, permission, thermal and degraded-network scenarios in a dedicated media target.

topics.title: watchOS, visionOS and specialized Apple platforms
topics.detail: The integration overview does not implement watch/immersive apps, spatial UI, companion transfer or each platform's distribution and input model.
topics.evidence: Create a platform-specific target and validate its independent lifecycle, interaction, storage and availability contracts.

topics.title: Bluetooth, nearby interaction and accessories
topics.detail: Discovery, connection restoration, protocol-level data, background limits and hardware testing need a separate curriculum.
topics.evidence: Implement and test a bounded device protocol including disconnect, restoration and denied authorization.

topics.title: HealthKit and regulated data integrations
topics.detail: App-domain familiarity is not authorization to process health data. Consent, entitlement, data handling and legal/privacy review need approved specialist ownership.
topics.evidence: Use synthetic data and an approved integration specification with privacy/security review before implementation.

topics.title: StoreKit, payments and transaction lifecycles
topics.detail: Purchase verification, entitlements, restore/refund behavior and changing store policies need current official guidance and dedicated tests.
topics.evidence: Implement a synthetic transaction flow with trusted verification, recovery and policy review.

topics.title: Document apps, CloudKit and conflict resolution
topics.detail: Document coordination, cloud sync, offline edits and multi-device conflicts are not established by a cache or Core Data overview.
topics.evidence: Define a conflict policy and reproduce concurrent offline edits and recovery in a separate sync lab.

topics.title: Core ML, model deployment and inference optimization
topics.detail: Model inputs, correctness/bias evaluation, on-device execution, resource budgets and model updates require separate evidence.
topics.evidence: Benchmark and validate a synthetic inference workload with explicit input and quality contracts.

topics.title: Network, credential and other specialist extensions
topics.detail: Widget/App Clip examples do not cover every extension point, special entitlement, interprocess contract or enterprise deployment model.
topics.evidence: Select an authorized extension point and test its process, entitlement, data and failure boundaries.

topics.title: Advanced Swift runtime and systems programming
topics.detail: Custom ownership/move-only APIs, unsafe pointers, C/C++ interop, compiler internals and low-level lock-free algorithms need deeper language-specific study.
topics.evidence: Prove a small low-level implementation's safety and behavior under dedicated compiler/runtime tests.
